items.headline: Flood Watch issued November 25 at 9:40PM EST until November 26 at 4:00PM EST by NWS Wakefield VA
items.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of southeast Maryland, including the following
areas, Dorchester, Inland Worcester, Maryland Beaches, Somerset and
Wicomico and Virginia, including the following areas, Accomack,
Eastern Essex, Eastern King William, Eastern King and Queen,
Gloucester, Lancaster, Mathews, Middlesex, Northampton,
Northumberland, Richmond, Western Essex, Western King William,
Western King and Queen and Westmoreland.

* WHEN...Through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Storm drains
and ditches may become clogged with debris.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Strong low pressure lifts northward overnight into the
Thanksgiving holiday. Widespread moderate to locally heavy
rainfall is expected over much of the area. Rainfall amounts of 3
to 5 inches are forecast, with localized higher totals of up to 6
inches possible.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
items.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

items.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 25 at 8:46PM EST until November 27 at 7:00AM EST by NWS Wakefield VA
items.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10
to 18 feet expected in the surf zone. For the Coastal Flood
Warning, 2 to 4 feet or more of inundation above ground level
expected in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...In Maryland, Maryland Beaches County. In Virginia,
Accomack County.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 7 AM EST Friday. For
the Coastal Flood Warning, from 5 AM to 5 PM EST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Major flooding is expected resulting in extreme
inundation. Water will be 2 to 4 feet or more above ground
level in flooded areas. Numerous homes and businesses could be
flooded. Many roads across the area may become impassable for
an extended period of time causing many neighborhoods to
become flooded and isolated. Life threatening flooding will
extend well inland from the waterfront and shoreline. Should
evacuations become necessary, follow the advice of local
officials for evacuation information.
items.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

items.headline: High Wind Warning issued November 25 at 7:17PM EST until November 26 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Wakefield VA
items.description:
* WHAT...East winds 35 to 45 mph with gusts up to 65 to 70 mph
expected. Locations along the immediate Atlantic coast have the
potential for peak gusts of 70 to 75 mph.

* WHERE...In Maryland, Dorchester, Inland Worcester, Maryland
Beaches, Somerset, and Wicomico Counties. In Virginia, Northampton
and Accomack Counties.

* WHEN...Until 7 PM EST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Damaging winds will blow down trees and power lines.
Widespread power outages are expected. Travel will be difficult,
especially for high profile vehicles.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The strongest winds are expected between 4 AM
and 12 PM EST Thursday.
items.instruction:
People are urged to secure loose objects that could be blown around
or damaged by the wind.

items.headline: Storm Warning issued November 25 at 6:51PM EST until November 26 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Wakefield VA
items.description:
* WHAT...East winds 40 to 50 kt with gusts up to 60 kt and seas
18 to 23 ft expected.

* WHERE...Coastal waters from Fenwick Island DE to Chincoteague
VA out 20 NM and Coastal waters from Chincoteague to Parramore
Island VA out 20 NM.

* WHEN...Until 7 PM EST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Storm force winds and hazardous seas will capsize or
damage vessels and reduce visibility.
items.instruction:
Mariners should remain in port, alter course, and/or secure the
vessel for severe conditions.
